_comment: THE AGENTIC HARNESS layer. Owner, 2026-09-20 (paraphrased): the harness, the content core above it and the composed checkout are distinct layers with distinct schemas — so this declares itself `cat-harness` rather than `folio-assistant`. It carried the latter until the repository root gained a harness.json of its own, at which point TWO layers declared one name and `instanceRoots` — keyed on the declared name — could only hold one of them. The one it held was the root, so `folio-assistant` resolved to the checkout and the harness layer became unreachable by name. `stub` was RENAMED to `cat-harness` on 2026-09-21 (owner ruling, PR #685), resolving the collision where both resolved to `<base>/folio-assistant.jsonld`. The CatHarness declaration for THIS layer — what directories it scans and what kind of graph each holds. See skills/kg/kg-core/directory-conventions.md. This repo is PRE-SPLIT (issue #223), so it declares what is true today, not the target layout: `tools/` and `folio/` do not exist here yet and are deliberately not declared. A directory that is declared but absent is worse than one that is missing, because every consumer then scans nothing and reports a clean run over it. NOTE: `schemas/` declares TWO graphs — the first real use of the array. A directory is a place to look and may hold more than one part of the graph; it does not say how to tell them apart, because the files declare what they are (see bean xxxb: schemas/*.ts does not yet do this well). `beans/` is declared ONCE, as a single `beans` graph. Its internal split — `defs` for work items, `workflows` for running BPMN state — is declared by `beans/beans.json`, not here. #263 declared the two as separate directories, one nested inside the other, which left a consumer unable to tell which owned what beneath it; the nodes now carry that.
_title: No `title`, deliberately: `displayTitle` is title || name || id, so the sidebar and the landing page fall back to `name` — which the schema already requires to be the layer's identifier, the one artefacts are stub-named after. A title here said `c@t-harness` and overrode that, labelling THIS repository with the brand of the harness layer that is still to be split out of it. Setting the title to `folio-assistant` instead would be the same fact in two fields, free to drift. The c@t-harness derivation stays in the description, where it is a tagline rather than an identity.

assets.description: The cold-start file for an agent working IN this layer, and it is THIS LAYER'S own as of 2026-09-20 (issue #592). It was declared `scope: "repository"`, so it resolved to the repository root's AGENTS.md — one file answering both "what binds everywhere" and "what binds in the harness layer", which is the conflation `readmeFinding` calls MAJOR for a non-root layer and could not report, because the asset DID resolve. assets.title: Initializing into folio-assistant
assets.description: What bootstrap's step 2 reads once it has been pointed at THIS layer. Published at the fixed convention every cat-harness layer honours, composed by `initializationDoc()` rather than spelled, so bootstrap needs no per-target knowledge and can initialise into a SPECIALISED harness it was never written against. Declared as an asset as well as conventional, so `check:declared-assets` verifies it is there and that its links resolve: a convention nothing checks is a convention that is honoured until it quietly is not. The path is INSTANCE-relative here, not `<stub>/docs/...`: this layer has its own directory (`cat-harness/`), so `siteDir` is plain `docs`, and the stub names published artefacts rather than a directory. Whether bootstrap can still find it from one reference is open — see bean `wggr`.

_stub_comment: RENAMED from `folio-assistant` on 2026-09-21, on the owner's ruling, closing the collision issue #649 raised and bean `x3bd` flagged as settle-before-you-move. `artefactStub(d) = d.stub ?? d.name`, so this field is the ONLY stub declared anywhere in the tree — every other layer falls through to its `name`. While it read `folio-assistant` it was the string the REPOSITORY ROOT layer also carries as its `name`, so both resolved to `<base>/folio-assistant.jsonld`: two vocabularies, one path, and a reader dereferencing it got whichever layer answered. It is kept as an explicit field rather than deleted so the rename is visible where the collision was, and because `x3bd` records that this string names published artefacts (`.jsonld`, `.schema.json`, the viewer directory) rather than being cosmetic.
_publication_comment: The `publication host` axis of docs/proposals/deployment-topologies.md, accepted 2026-09-19 (issue #363). WHAT KIND of host serves the renderings — distinct from `canonicalUrl` (the base @ids are minted against) and from `readme.linkStyle` in harness.config.json (how a link to a published artefact is written). This layer really does publish to GitHub Pages, so it declares so; a layer that has not said is `undefined`, which is a third state and must never be read as `github-pages`.

directories._coverage_comment: `docs` pointed at `cat-harness/docs/concepts/skills.md` until 2026-09-22 — a page titled "Skills & roles" whose headings are Skills, Roles and Capabilities, with no tools section in it. The tools graph had no documentation of its own and named a page about something else. That is worse than an absent ref, because an absent one is a legible gap while a ref that RESOLVES reports coverage: the check in force asks only whether the path exists, it did, and nothing ever flagged it. Found by applying the owner's instruction of 2026-09-21, "keep tools and skills separate!". `tool-graph.md` is the prose; `tools/index.md` is the generated view, and the two are different objects rather than two names for one.

One coordinated move", 2026-10-30): the loader (toolsFromFolders) and the shared helpers moved to the tools layer (https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness-tools/tree/main/schemas/tools) as schemas/tools/harness-tools.ts and schemas/tools/tool-helpers.ts, which is the path a consumer imports. The JSON-LD and JSON Schema renderings are generated.

The specifications this layer depends on, one record per specification, each pinning the EDITION in use and carrying the operative terms DERIVED from the corpus rather than hand-listed. Owner, 2026-09-20: "dont need to materalize, but should reference specific version being used" and "some schema that is operational should be in KG". UNDECLARED UNTIL 2026-09-22, which is the dh4f shape inverted: dh4f is a declared directory nothing holds, reported as a clean scan; this was a held directory nothing declared, so every consumer that fans out over declared directories skipped a registry that pins four external namespaces. It was reachable only by the one script that hardcodes its path. `dependents: reproduce` because a dependent folio consumes its own specifications — it inherits the convention, an id and a relative path, not this layer's records.

coverage._visualiser_comment: Declared 2026-09-23 under bean `yunp`: `external-schema` was one of the kinds with no published viewer, so the navbar listed it disabled and four records — an authority, an edition, its namespace IRIs, its dependents and its operative terms each — were reachable only by opening the JSON. ADDED TO THE COVERAGE BLOCK THAT WAS ALREADY HERE, not beside it: the first attempt wrote a second `coverage` key into the same object, which JSON permits and every parser resolves by taking the last — so the visualiser was silently discarded and the generator reported `no visualiser declared`. A duplicate key is not a merge.

directories.title: Subscribed substrates
directories.description: The root declaration of each Knowledge Graph this layer subscribes to, cached at the pinned commit: one `<id>.substrate.json` per `subscriptions` entry, holding the upstream bytes, their sha256, and the harnesses and subgraphs the substrate offers. Written by `bun run cat kg:subscribe`; never edited by hand. Each CHOSEN part a subscriber materialises lands here too, under `<id>/subgraphs/<subgraph>/` or `<id>/assets/<path>/`: the upstream bytes under `tree/` and a `materialization.json` beside them with fixity, provenance and the five gates. A subgraph fetched in metadata mode (`kg:materialize --nodes`) lands under `<id>/nodes/<subgraph path>/`: its published `index.hydrated.jsonld` and a `nodes.json` record with its sha256. Written by `bun run cat kg:materialize`; never edited by hand. Nothing else writes here: an instantiated harness's state lives in `subscribed-harnesses/` (owner, 2026-10-30, bean `w1gy` finding 1, option C, "split the directory").
directories.readOnlyBasis: Copies of somebody else's bytes at a pin: each snapshot carries the sha256 of the upstream declaration it wraps, and each materialised part a `materialization.json` with fixity per file, re-checked by `kg:subscribe:check`, `kg:materialize:check` and `check:materialized-fixity`. Refresh by moving the pin and re-running the writer, never by editing here. The subscriber's own working state was split out to `subscribed-harnesses/` so this directory holds copies only.
directories._description_comment: Issue #1719, epic bean `fnx4`, slice 4. A NEW directory rather than a reused one because no declared kind fits: `external-schema` is a person's decision about an edition (`content`), `library` is ingested L1 sections, and `catalogue` is core's, which cat-harness may not depend on. The snapshot is somebody else's bytes regenerated by a command, which is `derived`. `dependents: skip` because a subscription is a choice each layer makes for itself: `reproduce` would put an empty directory in every downstream folio, and one that subscribes declares its own (`kg:subscribe` refuses a layer that declares none, and says what to declare). The snapshot WRAPS the upstream `<name>.json` rather than copying it, because a bare copy carries `name` equal to its stem, which is the rule every scanner uses to recognise a layer declaration.

directories.title: Subscribed harness state
directories.description: The state directories of each harness this layer instantiates from a KG subscription: `<subscription>/<harness>/<state path>/`, one home per chosen harness, each state directory the harness declares created with a `.gitkeep`. Written by `bun run cat kg:instantiate`; the harness's processes write into it after that. Never at the repository root, where a harness named after a staged layer would write into that layer's directory (gap G11), and never under `subscriptions/`, which holds upstream's bytes and is read-only.
directories._description_comment: Owner, 2026-10-30 22:37Z (bean `w1gy` finding 1, option C, "split the directory"): the state `kg:instantiate` wrote under `subscriptions/<id>/harnesses/` made one directory both upstream's copies and the subscriber's working state, so `check:read-only-graphs` could not be answered either way. The copies stay in `subscriptions/` (read-only); the state moves here, under the `subscribed-harnesses` graph typology (`holds: state`). It holds only its README today: cat-harness's one subscription, `ihris`, chooses no harness, by the owner's ruling recorded in `_subscriptions_comment`. `dependents: skip`, for the reason `subscriptions` gives: a subscription is each layer's own choice.
directories.readOnlyBasis: The subscriber's own working state: `kg:instantiate` makes each home and the subscribed harness's processes write into it. Nothing here is a copy of upstream's bytes.
directories._source_comment: MOUNTED, 2026-10-31 (fa#2781): the typology `holds: state`, and `check:state-on-main` refuses new state on `main`, so it is kept on its own per-graph branch like beans, todos and issue-marks (owner, 2026-10-03, bean laqs) and mounted here by `bun run cat state:mount`. Main dropped it in the same commit that declared this source, because `mountTip` refuses a path the checkout still tracks.

directories.description: Closed sets of codes, one `"$schema": "folio-code-list/v1"` file per list, each code carrying a label, a definition, a source and, where it stands for one, a value. Owner, 2026-09-23: "we need an expandable option, not just declared in code. list of codes and corresponding narrative desc and source should be part of a node/asset", and SKOS as the published form. Two consumers today: adjudication steps name the list their `codes` come from (`<folio:adjudication list="…">`, checked when a diagram loads), and `schemas/kg/namespaces.ts` reads every namespace this project mints from `own-namespaces.json` instead of carrying them as constants. Exported as SKOS concept schemes to `_kg/<stub>-code-lists.jsonld` by `scripts/glossary-export.ts`, beside the swimlane glossary. `dependents: skip` — a dependent INHERITS these through the dependency overlay (`codeListDirs`), and declares its own directory only when it has a list of its own.

Vocabulary mappings: one `"$schema": "folio-vocab-mapping/v1"` table per source content type and target node, saying which source field becomes which target predicate and with what relationship. A table is shaped like a FHIR ConceptMap, so an existing ConceptMap is representable here and a table can be produced as one, with the loss reported (`schemas/vocab-mapping-fhir.ts`). Owner, 2026-09-23 (bean sl9u): "need Tools for this type of ETL procedure depending on source / target content type and other metadata". Ruled 2026-10-02 (bean k74z): option 1, tables as KG data applied by the in-process `vocab-map` Tool. First consumer: `scripts/glossary-export.ts`. `dependents: skip`: a table belongs to the Tool that applies it, which lives here.

directories.title: Tool releases
directories.description: The external tools this platform runs: one `folio-tool-release/v1` file per tool at one version, with the sha256 of its bytes, where to fetch it, its SPDX licence, how to run it and the runtimes that release needs; and one `folio-tool-profile/v1` file per named set of releases a run selects. A profile never names a runtime.
directories._description_comment: Issue #2481, bean `3sbm`, step 1 of `docs/proposals/tool-releases-2026-10-07.md`. Owner 2026-10-07, T1 = (a): releases and profiles live in cat-harness as a declared graph that every layer inherits, so a dependent reads this directory through the dependency overlay and declares none of its own. T4 = (a): the first tools are PlantUML with its JRE, and graphviz. Every digest here was computed over downloaded bytes or read from the publisher's checksum file, never written down from memory. A profile file is `<name>.profile.json` and a release file is `<name>-<version>[-<platform>].json`, so no file's stem equals its `name` field, which is the rule `findDeclarationFile` uses to recognise a layer declaration. Run contexts (`folio-run-context/v1`) are produced per run and are not kept here.

directories.description: The per-skill JSON Schemas and the schema documents the harness declares. Since bean 8lcl (owner card "A. One coordinated move", 2026-10-30) the Zod sources of the content-object model live in the tools layer (https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness-tools/tree/main/schemas); this directory keeps the data. Declares BOTH graphs: the schema definitions themselves, and `kg` because a schema IS a knowledge-graph node.

The JSON-LD @contexts this layer publishes, one per namespace, served at `<iriBase>ns/<name>/v1.jsonld`: `content/` (the shared content context, written by `scripts/gen-jsonld-context.ts`) and `subgraph/` (the subgraph context the docs JSON-LD names). Both are committed. `context/v1.jsonld`, the layer context, is NOT committed and stays listed under `builtAtPublish`, because it is computed over the checkout's other layers. Declared 2026-10-24 under bean `0uu2` (owner, card "A. Declare and keep"): before this only `ns/context/v1.jsonld` was named, so the two committed contexts sat in a present-but-undeclared directory that no consumer scanning the declaration could see.

UML class diagrams of every named sub-graph a harness declares — uml/overview/<instance>.puml|.mmd and uml/overview/<instance>/<sub-graph>.puml|.mmd — written from one model by scripts/gen-uml-overview.ts. The groupings are the declaration entries themselves and the classes are read from each graph typology's registered validator, so nothing here is authored. The rendered pages are docs/uml/overview/, which show the PlantUML rendering (docs/assets/img/uml/overview/, stamped with its source's hash) with the Mermaid beneath it, and link both sources. Owner, 2026-09-23.

directories.readOnlyBasis: NOT frozen, and the exception is worth stating. Most of this graph is authored here and edited every day. Since issue #556 it also holds the skill packages synced from a remote package at a pinned commit: each carries its own `materialization.json` with a sha256 per file, so `check:materialized-fixity` already fails an edit in place, file by file. Freezing the whole directory because some packages in it are materialized would freeze the skills this repository writes.
directories.description: The knowledge graph. Skill packages, and the four other node kinds that point at them: `roles/roles.json` (a role IS a BPMN swimlane, and carries the skills its lane's activities need), `workflows/*.bpmn` + `workflows/decisions/*.dmn` (the processes those roles act in, reached through the skill that describes them), `requirements/*.json` (conformance obligations whose `satisfiedBy` names the skill or capability discharging them), `permissions/permissions.json` (what an actor may DO in any lane, as opposed to what its lane's role knows), Its audit verdicts are NOT here: they moved to the `qa` tree on 2026-09-19, because a verdict is a QA reviewer's output and placement follows provenance. Its id is `skills`, so its qualified name is `cat-harness.skills`; it was `cat-harness` until 2026-09-23 (bean iwtn), and `resolveDirectories` still reads that id as this one. Ids are stable across a relocation, paths are not. The `skills` graph does NOT owe a visualiser: `owesVisualiser` is `!renderable && holds !== "content"`, and `skills` is `content` — *"a graph that stands on its own does not need a viewer to be legible"*. So no gate was failing. What WAS wrong is that the viewer already existed and nothing declared it: `auto-docs` renders one sub-page per skills directory, and `graph-tiles.undeclaredProjections` lists exactly a directory with a published page and no declared visualisation — so all seven read as "no published viewer" in the navbar tiles while being rendered the whole time. `tools` is the same `content` kind and has declared one all along, which is the precedent: declaring a visualiser for a content kind is a courtesy the corpus already extends, not an obligation this invents.

Scenarios — the Roles an Actor takes on, in `roles.json`, and the User Stories told as them, in `stories.json`. A Role IS a BPMN swimlane: it carries the Skills its lane's activities need and the Actor kinds that may play it; a lane names its Role, and a story names the Role it is told as, so the Role lists neither (#1168). SPLIT OUT OF `skills/` on 2026-09-21 so that "give me the Scenarios" is a query on the kind rather than a match on a path.

What an Actor may DO, as W3C ODRL 2.2 policies (issue #1180, owner 2026-09-23). `folio-defaults.jsonld` is the layer's odrl:Set: the permissions each actor file used to list, migrated one rule per (actor, action), plus the owner's floor for an unauthenticated reader (visualize and render only). Actions are the folio ODRL profile in `skills/permissions/permissions.json`; roles stay in `scenarios/`, and identity (which login is which actor) stays in the data store, never here. `dependents: skip` because a downstream layer writes its own policies and inherits these through ODRL's `inheritFrom`, rather than getting a copy.

Executable BPMN processes and the DMN tables their gateways compute from. The diagrams are the source of truth, not illustrations of one: a lane binds a Role, an activity names the Skill to run through `<folio:skill ref>`, and `workflow_complete` refuses a step that is not enabled. WHERE A RUNNING INSTANCE GOT TO is not here — that is `beans/workflows/`, kind `workflow-state`, which is `state` rather than `content`. Two questions, two graphs. GROUPED BY CONCERN since placement PR3 (bean `63wl`): `processes.json` names the groups, each diagram sits in `processes/<group>/` and a DMN in `processes/<group>/decisions/` beside the diagrams that read it; the content-type diagrams moved up to the layers that own their skills (folio-assistant-core, folio-assistant-sci, fhir-harness), whose same-named `processes/<group>/` are members of these groups.

coverage._visualiser_comment: THE LIST FORM, so the entry can carry a title. Declared 2026-09-23 under bean `yunp`: `methodology` was one of seven kinds with no published viewer, which the build reports as a finding in `_data/harness.json` and the navbar renders as a disabled row. The page spans EVERY declared methodology graph, not this directory alone — a DAK layer's `methodologies/` and the content core's are the same kind and their nodes are on it, labelled by declaring layer. So the visualiser is declared once, here, rather than three times at one page: the obligation is per KIND and a second declaration would be a second claim on one file.

directories.description: Judgement methodologies the harness owns, one sub-graph each: Kepner-Tregoe for a decision, MADR for its record, DMN for the computable case. PARALLEL rather than composable — which applies is contextual, and blending them produces a house method that cites nobody. Its own graph typology rather than skills, for three properties a skill does not have: extractable (somebody else's work, adopted, so it lifts out with its declaration when the field moves on), referenced rather than inlined (two skills quoting one method is two copies free to drift), and exempt from skill criteria (skill-is-brief caps an INSTRUCTION near 280 lines; a methodology is a faithful rendering of an external standard, and truncating it to fit a house limit would misrepresent the standard). GRADE is deliberately NOT here: it is WHO guideline method, and since 2026-09-24 (bean `wg7r`) it is the `grade` skill in the DAK layer's `skills/content/authoring-who-smart-guidelines/` with its vocabularies as code lists — the owner: "needs to be part of skill/SKOS etc. … dont want smart-kg here yet, that is its own repo already". RELOCATION, 2026-09-22, and the THREE declarations it removed. The owner: "dont bury sub-graph assets. same for <stub>/skills, etc." CRDM's three skills moved to `skills/process/crdm/`, RACI's to `skills/process/raci/`, and CRDM's eight diagrams to `processes/` — the stub-level graphs that were already declared. `methodology-crdm`, `methodology-raci` and `methodology-crdm-processes` are GONE rather than repointed: a separate entry for a directory that is already a package subdirectory of the declared `skills/` graph would declare one directory twice, which is the `x4v4` graph-inside-a-graph shape one level down. `gen-skill-docs` demonstrated it rather than anyone reasoning it out — it demanded a category under BOTH the basename and the declaration id, because both discovery branches found the same directory. So this entry now has the `methodology` graph to itself, holding exactly the four nodes and no subgraph: dmn, kepner-tregoe, madr, swot. This REVERSES the placement half of bean `g43o`; its argument that a reader should meet CRDM as a thing rather than as three prefixed filenames is preserved by the package manifest, which is what makes a skill package a thing everywhere else in this tree.

Everything a QA process produced, in one declared tree. The owner's rule, 2026-09-19: an artefact generated primarily as a QA reviewer belongs under `test/results/` as part of a QA process — placement follows PROVENANCE, not file family and not who fetches it afterwards. Four kinds live here and the FILES say which they are, per the `$schema` contract: `qa-results/v1` (`<producer>.qa-results.json`, a whole-artefact review — findings about a document the build just produced), `qa-witness/v1` (`witnesses/**`, one per audited subject in the families `block`, `kg` and `translation`, the published projection) `kg-qa/v1` (`kg-qa/**`, the KG verdicts themselves — what `kg-audit` wrote) and `kg-qa-manifest/v1` (`kg-qa.manifest.json`, the auditor's identity for all of them, ONE per layer rather than one per sidecar). The manifest moved here from `skills/` on 2026-09-27: `kg-audit.ts` writes it unconditionally, so auditing every declared layer made its old home CREATE a `skills/` directory holding no skills in each of the six layers that have none. Its registration in `graph-typology-registry.ts` moved from the `skills` kind to `qa` with it — a kind claiming a `$schema` whose files live in another kind's directory is a validator aimed at nothing. The `kg-qa/` tree MIRRORS each subject's path rather than being flat, and that is not tidiness: measured 2026-09-19, four sidecar basenames already occur twice across packages (`editor`, `getting-started`, `idle-backlog`, `l2-dak-authoring`), so a flat directory would silently overwrite four verdicts. `kgQaSidecarPath` in `schemas/sdlc/kg-qa.ts` is the one answer for writer and reader alike. A directory is a PLACE TO LOOK and may hold more than one part of a graph; extension is a coincidence, a declaration inside the file is the contract. ONE entry rather than a nested set, deliberately: #263's own comment names the defect a declaration inside another declaration creates. STILL OUTSIDE: the 122 block verdicts `*.qa.json`, which sit beside their blocks and move next. The witnesses are PUBLISHED at `/assets/qa/`, which is where every badge points; the publishing workflows copy them into `_site/assets/qa/` after Jekyll, since Jekyll builds only `docs/`. Where a file lives and where it is served from are different questions.

The JUDGEMENT half of every QA verdict this layer carries across runs, split out of `test/results/` by owner ruling D2 (a), 2026-10-01 (bean `2gst`, arc `3fva`): derived script verdicts move to the `qa-reports` branch; anything a reviewer judged stays HERE, on main, where a `git rm` of derived results cannot reach it. One `qa-attestations/v1` file per subject at `<family>/<mirrored subject path>.attestations.json`, where `<family>` is the derived family it sits beside (`kg-qa`, bean `2gst`; `block-qa` and `translation-qa`, bean `8wj1`) and the mirror is exactly that family's own, so a subject's attestation is found by swapping the tree root and the suffix. Today: the `pair_attestations` that were carried inside `kg-qa/v1` sidecars, ALL of them, the `by: baseline` entries with the `by: agent` ones; the owner ruled on 2026-10-01 that a baseline is a judgement, because a regenerated one forgets the drift it recorded (defect C4). `voice_reviews` live here too when one is recorded. Under `adversarial-review/`: the `adversarial_reviews` that `adversarial-backfill` or a reviewer recorded about a tool, schema, skill or process, on the `kg-qa` mirror, pinned by the subject's `source_hash` (owner, 2026-10-14: carry them forward; they sat only in the derived sidecars, so #857 took the last two, restored here verbatim from 161b243^). Under `block-qa/` and `translation-qa/`: every block or translation verdict whose `reviewer.kind` is not `script` (13 at the split, 11 + 2), held in a `criteria` map of the derived report's own shape; the derived report keeps a projection composed from here. Schema and the five read states (hit / miss / absent / corrupt / unknown): `schemas/sdlc/qa-attestations.ts`. Owner ruling 2 (2026-10-01): a writer that finds judgements in a prior derived file and no store entry MOVES them here as it saves, rather than refusing; a corrupt store is still unknown and refused. Hosted layers (bootstrap) would sit under `<stub>/`, as their `qa` verdicts do. Declared WITH its files, per bean dh4f.

Test plans this layer certifies against — one `test-plan/v1` document per plan (`schemas/sdlc/test-plan.ts`). Content, not state: a process reads a plan and never writes it, and the run points at the plan, never the reverse. The runs and reports a plan's execution produces go to the `qa-reports` branch with the rest of `test/results/`, and the certification decision to `test/attestations/` (owner ruling D2). First declared for dogfood plan #1, `crdm-detect-evaluation` (bean `folio-assistant-ff09`). Declared WITH its files, per bean dh4f.

Repository health reports — what the daily sweep under `test/health/` wrote. One `health-report/v1` document, declaring itself with a `$schema` tag rather than being duck-typed by path: a directory is a PLACE TO LOOK and the files inside say what they are. A SEPARATE graph from `qa`, and the line between them is about the SUBJECT, not the producer: a QA verdict judges an artefact this repository produced, against criteria that artefact is supposed to meet; a health report judges the REPOSITORY ITSELF — how big it has grown, how much of the publish branch the review previews occupy, whether the work plan has duplicates in it. Folding it into `qa` would leave a consumer asking for verdicts about this layer's content holding a fact about its clone. NOTE the path: it was `tests/health/results/` when this graph landed in #395, because this repository then had BOTH `test/` (the `qa` graph) and `tests/` (the Playwright e2e specs), and the owner asked for `tests/health`. #395 flagged that inconsistency in `skills/kg/kg-core/directory-conventions.md` rather than resolving it, since relocating a declared directory as a side effect of adding a check is the `dh4f` shape, where a consumer scans nothing and reports a clean run over it. The owner settled it on `test/` the same day and it moved as its own change — bean `auap`, PR #400. The `id` here is unchanged, deliberately: an inheriting layer overrides on the entry's id and never on its path, so `health` still binds after the relocation. The e2e specs came to the declaration rather than the declaration to the specs, because `testDir` is one line of one config file and a declared path is what every downstream override resolves against.
directories._scope_comment: REPOSITORY-scoped, like `beans` and `todos` (owner, 2026-10-23, bean folio-assistant-kyrg: "Yes, scope: repository"). A health report is about the REPOSITORY the sweep runs in, so whatever checkout mounts this harness keeps it at its own root, on its own origin's `cat/cat-harness/health`. Unscoped, it bound to the mounted cat-harness layer, so the index's daily sweep pushed to litlfred/cat-harness's branch, which that workflow's token cannot write: a 403 on every run. Standalone, this checkout IS the root, so nothing here moves.
directories._source_comment: MOUNTED, owner 2026-10-11 (session_01UC1NuEuSy1MBNpEhnDuiGj, 05:58:12Z: "move health to state branch now"). The report is generated state, not reviewed content, so it is kept on its own per-graph branch (owner, 2026-10-03, bean laqs) and mounted at this path by `bun run cat state:mount`; main dropped it in the same commit that declared this source, because `mountTip` refuses a path the checkout still tracks.

coverage._visualiser_comment: ITS OWN HARNESS, not the library viewer. Both entries declared this same path until 2026-09-21, so the uploads tile opened the corpus browser and rendered the library's entry count — 0 here, while 27 sources waited in the queue beside it. Bean v18c tabled three ways to divide one page; the owner rejected all three: "uploads/ are not ingested, they are ingested into libray/ ... funcionally different/behavior diffent so need distinct harness". gen-library-viz reads bib-slugs, sections/, structure.json and the OCR three-state, none of which a queue has. The two are STAGES of one pipeline (see uploads-and-library-are-two-stages-of-one-pipeline.md), and this view exists to show what is NOT in the library — which the library viewer cannot do by construction.

directories.description: The incoming queue of the document-ingestion pipeline — raw files as dropped, before ingestion. NOT L1 and NOT greppable as corpus: the corpus checklist searches library/ only, so a source still sitting here reads as absent to every consumer while the file is on disk. That is why it is a separate declaration from library/ rather than the same directory under two names.

directories.title: Library
directories.description: The library sub-graph — a NAMED SUB-GRAPH of the harness on the pattern of `sdlc/` and `openapi/`, holding everything about libraries: the skills that teach acquisition, ingestion, cataloguing, translation and materialisation (`library-core`, `large-datasets`), the processes that run them, with their decision tables, and this layer's own corpus of cited sources. The graphs inside it — `library-skills`, `library-processes` and `library` — are declared FROM WITHIN, in `library/graph.json` (#980). The sub-graph itself is ON in every layer, because the content layers ingest with its skills and call its processes; only the corpus inside it is OPT-IN (owner, 2026-11-04, card 'Library cut' option 1: the skills and processes always on, the corpus opt-in). The id is not `library` on purpose: a layer above that declares its own `library` replaces an inherited entry of that id, and would take this sub-graph's skills and processes with it.

coverage._visualiser_comment: Bean lnur. This graph owed a visualiser and kg:audit said so — cat-harness declares several graphs with no published viewer and this was one. Generated by scripts/gen-translation-status.ts, which measures the .pot/.po files on each run. NOT a state-visualizer dashboard: that generator draws only STATE graphs, and translation-sources is the INPUT to injection rather than something a process writes as it runs, so it is correctly skipped there and always will be.

directories.description: The gettext side of translation — one directory per target locale holding `.pot` templates, `.po` catalogues and the `TranslationNode` `.ts` manifests that make each pair addressable in the graph. The INPUT to injection. There is deliberately NO matching declaration for the rendered OUTPUT: a translated page is the same kind of thing as the page it translates — renderable content, differing by a field — and it declares its own `lang` and `translation_source` in front matter, so the locale subtrees under `docs/` are DISCOVERED from the files rather than enumerated here. A first draft of PR #351 enumerated them, ten entries for five locales across two subtrees, and that restated what all ten files already said. Undeclared until 2026-09-19: the `dh4f` defect in reverse, five committed directories that no declaration mentioned.

coverage._visualiser_comment: Bean 7ofc, on the owner's ruling of 2026-09-22: "folio must be in cat-harness and visualizer owned by it". `folio` is the only renderable kind — its CONTENT already comes out as the landing board via gen-landing-data — so check:subgraph-coverage never asked for this and owesVisualiser exempts the kind, exactly as it exempted library (jbx2) and voices (bu2q). What had no view was the GRAPH: which nodes exist, what each anchors to, its theme, where it was declared, and the links it carries. Generated by scripts/gen-folio-viz.ts, which re-reads the directories on every run and gives a declared-but-absent one a ROW rather than silence.

directories.description: Authored content of this layer itself, rendered to a website. Holds the landing sticky — the layer's own description and its onboarding links, as a page-global note rather than text composited into the backdrop.

The harness's own minimal folio renderer (bean ohx6, owner ruling 2026-10-10): `file-list.ts`, which renders the folio as the list of files it holds into `folio/index.md`, and the skill that says when to run it. Code and a skill, not folio content: the folio reader reads only `folio/*.json`, and the renderer skips this directory.

The SITE CHROME: the just-the-docs theme configuration (`_config.yml`'s theme keys, the `Gemfile`), the generic includes every page pulls in (`head_custom`, `footer_custom`, `nav_footer_custom`, `mermaid_config`) and the stylesheets and scripts they load, in their Jekyll-relative places. Concern group `ui`. It is the BASE layer of the composed docs tree: declared BEFORE `docs`, so `compose-docs` lays it down first and `docs/` overlays it (later wins; `_config.yml` merged, parse-equal to the file it was cut from, ruling D1). Empty `_includes/generated/*` stand-ins let a site with no harness pages build. A downstream that wants the harness's look without its 3,456 pages mounts `site-chrome` and omits `docs`. Owner, 2026-10-09: *"go ahead with the cat-harness chrome subgraph"*; proposal `docs/proposals/semantic-subgraphs-2026-10-09.md`, slice 1. directories._description_comment: Documentation ABOUT the knowledge graph itself -- 241 markdown files, the entire published surface, and UNDECLARED until 2026-09-20. That is the dh4f defect in its purest form: every declaration-driven consumer scanned straight past the thing readers actually see. Owner, same day: 'docs/ is about documentation about the KG itself... docs/ in cat-harness', with the intent that this is WHERE DOCUMENTATION GOES and therefore the only place a forward reference may be authored. The `docs` kind is RENDERABLE and is registered by `schemas/docs-graph-typology.ts` rather than added to BASE_GRAPH_TYPOLOGIES, so the assertion that the harness's base vocabulary carries no renderable kind stays true and its test stays unchanged. Distinct from `folio`, which is core's: the difference is the SUBJECT. A page explaining how ingestion works is `docs`; a note an author writes about an ingested catalogue is a `folio`; the catalogue itself is `library/`. `dependents` is `skip`, unlike the other renderable graph `folio`: this is documentation THIS layer publishes about the knowledge graph, so a dependent folio inherits the pages rather than an empty directory to refill — it authors its own subject matter under `folio/`, which is `reproduce`. CHANGED TO `reproduce` 2026-09-21 ON THE OWNER'S COMPOSE RULING (bean `n0nf`, issue #638), and the paragraph above is kept rather than deleted because its reasoning was right for the question it answered. It argued `skip` on the grounds that a dependent should INHERIT THE PAGES rather than get an empty directory to refill. Under compose it gets BOTH: the pages still reach it, and `reproduce` gives it the place to override one. So this is not a reversal of that argument, it is the second half of it arriving. The `dependents` doc warns that defaulting to `reproduce` ships junk -- twelve inherited directories, four of them the platform's own, each empty with a committed keep marker, the `dh4f` shape shipped downstream. That warning is about a DEFAULT, and the test it turns on is the one that schema states: is this directory part of the SHAPE a folio has, or merely where THIS layer's content lives? Before the ruling `docs/` was the second. After it, a folio is expected to author and override its own documentation, which makes it the first -- the same answer `uploads/` and `library/` get, and they are `reproduce` and also start empty. WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO is give the REPOSITORY ROOT a `docs/`. The root does not depend on cat-harness (measured: its declaration chain has length 1), so nothing is inherited there, and the root's own `harness.json` carries the owner's "only uploads/ on this repo's root". `n0nf` says the root's docs "is not its own: cat-harness installs it", which needs a dependency edge that does not exist. That is left for the owner rather than settled here. A viewer IS declared for this `docs` directory, and `owesVisualiser` not demanding one is not the same as forbidding one. The kind is `renderable`, so it does not OWE a viewer — but the owner's rule, quoted in full in `mount-instance-docs.ts`'s module note, is that a harness which instantiates a directory MAKES a visualiser for it, docs and library included. It points at the `auto-docs` index, NOT at the mount route `/docs/<instance>/`: that mount is a VERBATIM copy of the directory, and `visualiserHref` exists precisely because linking a rail to it lands on a byte-identical page — the owner's report that clicking `doc/` under a layer's navbar did nothing. The owner's sentence is CITED rather than quoted here on purpose: it names a graph whose viewer is `publish: "staging-only"`, and a test asserts that name appears NOWHERE in the built export — including in a declaration's own prose, which is where quoting it put it. The test caught that, and this paragraph is the second attempt.

_needs_comment: The layer this layer sits on. Owner, 2026-09-20: "So bootsteap, cat harness, fa-core, f-a, from bottom to top." Declared rather than hardcoded in the navbar, so the ordering is a fact of the repository and not of whichever consumer needed it first. `bootstrap-tools` added 2026-09-30 (bean `0lj4`, owner's ruling): bean `xsqm` moved that code OUT of this layer into its own, and this list was not updated with it, so 20 imports under `cat-harness/` reached a layer this file did not name. `allowedFromNeeds` gives a layer `{layer} U ancestors(layer)`, and `bootstrap-tools` is a SIBLING of `cat-harness` rather than an ancestor, so every one of those 20 was `wrong-direction` by the declared rule while four separate checks reported clean. The reverse arrow stays forbidden and is guarded by `check:tools-closure`. REMOVED again 2026-10-30 (bean `8lcl`, owner card "A. One coordinated move"): the code those imports sat in moved to cat-harness-tools, which names `bootstrap-tools` in its own `needs`. Measured after the move, no file under `cat-harness/` imports `bootstrap-tools`, so the edge named nothing.
_jsonldPrefixes_comment: The external vocabularies this layer's JSON-LD speaks (schemas/kg/jsonld-prefixes.ts; bean folio-assistant-63q4, owner 2026-10-14). Measured 2026-10-14: these are emitted (doco, prov, dcterms by the block/library/site generators; skos by the glossary export; cito by block siblings; rdfs by the named-subgraph documents, through ns/subgraph/v1.jsonld's aliases). deo, oa, csvw and fhir are bound in CONTENT_CONTEXT but emitted by no code and no document, so they are not declared: the generated context will not carry them.
_cat_bootstrap_comment: NO `bootstrap` DIRECTORY IS DECLARED HERE, and that is the owner's ruling of 2026-09-21 ("neither") on bean `pve3`, not an omission. This file used to declare `bootstrap/skills/` with `scope: "repository"`, which resolves against the REPOSITORY root rather than this instance — so bootstrap's skills and roles landed in folio-assistant's graph while the entry lived here. It did NOT declare `bootstrap/workflows/`, deliberately, because #432 measured bootstrap's process leaking into the root graph 88 times. The root therefore carried HALF of bootstrap, and the two symptoms were one asymmetry: a `lanes` entry on a bootstrap role minted `bindsLane -> role/<Lane>` pointing at a lane node only bootstrap's own export mints (four dangling links, measured 2026-09-21 by restoring `lanes` and watching `kg-export.test.ts` refuse it), and bootstrap's `kg-navigation` collided by name with `skills/folio-core/kg-navigation` in the published docs (bean `v3se`). `pve3` put the choice as BOTH halves or NEITHER; both would undo #432's isolation and put a process the root does not own into its published graph. Under NEITHER, bootstrap's skills are published through `bootstrap.jsonld` and its own instance page, which is where an instance's own graph belongs. The old entry's rationale is preserved in the bean rather than here, because a rationale for a declaration that no longer exists reads as a declaration to a skimming reader.
